A.explanation: This is the magnitude of the vertical component alone at $9.00\text{ s}$, $|v_y| = 6.58\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and it omits the $4.00\text{ m s}^{-1}$ horizontal component.

B.explanation: The vertical component becomes $-6.58\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and combined with $4.00\text{ m s}^{-1}$ horizontally by Pythagoras gives $7.70\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: This adds the component magnitudes $6.58 + 4.00$ linearly instead of combining perpendicular vectors with $v = \sqrt{v_x^2+v_y^2}$.

D.explanation: This is approximately $gt = 1.62 \times 9.00 = 14.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the change in vertical velocity, ignoring the $8.00\text{ m s}^{-1}$ initial upward velocity and the horizontal motion.

hints: Notice the two separate motions: the horizontal component stays at $4.00\text{ m s}^{-1}$ because there is no air resistance, while the vertical component is changed by lunar gravity.
Use $v_y = u_y - gt$ for the vertical direction with $u_y = 8.00\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $g = 1.62\text{ m s}^{-2}$, taking upward as positive so the result can become negative on the way down.
Combine the final perpendicular components with Pythagoras, $v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2}$, rather than adding them directly.
walkthrough: Treat horizontal and vertical separately. With no air resistance, $v_x$ stays constant at $4.00\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for the whole $9.00\text{ s}$.
For vertical motion use $v_y = u_y - gt$ with upward positive. Substitute $u_y = 8.00\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $g = 1.62\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and $t = 9.00\text{ s}$.
Calculate $v_y = 8.00 - (1.62 \times 9.00) = 8.00 - 14.58 = -6.58\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The negative sign means the ball is moving downward at $6.58\text{ m s}^{-1}$ vertically.
Speed is the magnitude of the resultant velocity, so use Pythagoras: $v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{(4.00)^2 + (-6.58)^2}$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
Evaluate: $v = \sqrt{16.0 + 43.30} = \sqrt{59.30} \approx 7.70\text{ m s}^{-1}$. This is option B.
